R501.note: resolve().normalize() plus startsWith(base) containment check is the right shape; only escaping paths now get 403 and legitimate downloads are unchanged.

R502.note: std::array::at() throws std::out_of_range for slot >= 32, which satisfies the contract's reject-or-report requirement and leaves valid slots and the Badge shape unchanged.

R503.note: Switching to '%s' lazy formatting does not neutralize anything - reproduced in scratch with Python 3.13: a username containing a newline still produces a forged second log line, so the CWE-117 vector is untouched and the explanation's neutralization claim is false; nothing else changed.

R504.note: JSON.parse closes the node-serialize function-eval RCE and node-serialize's own output for data objects is plain JSON so existing cookies still parse; the invalid-JSON/non-object fallback to {} matches the code's existing empty-profile default and is stated.

R505.note: PasswordEncoder.matches() against UserDetails.getPassword() with BadCredentialsException on mismatch is the DaoAuthenticationProvider shape; the new constructor dependency on a PasswordEncoder bean is stated and is inherent to the fix.

R506.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode() correctly closes the body-context XSS, but it throws ArgumentNullException on null (reproduced in scratch on .NET 10), so a request missing orderId or note - which the original rendered fine as an empty value - now 500s, and the write-up does not mention it.

R507.note: Replacing the shell listing with Files.list() removes the injection surface, but the fix prints each filename to stdout where the original discarded process output (the 'preserving original behavior' claim is wrong), and a missing/non-directory path now throws NoSuchFileException where the original returned quietly after a failed ls.

R508.note: Argument-array exec.Command with no sh -c makes both paths literal argv entries as the contract requires; a leading '-' in a path could still be read as a convert option, but that is outside the stated contract and pre-existed.

R509.note: HttpUtility.JavaScriptStringEncode is the correct encoder for a JS string-literal context in System.Web (escapes quotes, backslash, <, >, line terminators) and returns empty string for null exactly as the original concatenation did.

R510.note: extractall(filter=tarfile.data_filter) is the vendor-prescribed PEP 706 fix and is live on the stated python:3.11 image (3.11.4+); the hasattr fallback with its '..' substring test and no symlink check is weaker but is dead code on any current 3.11 patch release.

R511.note: Dropping cmd.exe /c and passing -n, 4 and host via ArgumentList to ping.exe makes host a literal argv entry, and output/exit handling is unchanged; option injection via a host beginning with '-' (e.g. -t) remains but pre-existed and is not the reported vector.

R512.note: unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes' => false]) is the format-preserving fix, so rows written before any migration still load and no cart is lost; only if legacy carts held objects would items surface as __PHP_Incomplete_Class, which the write-up's 'primitive types' wording implicitly acknowledges.

R513.note: Build FAIL: SandboxedEnvironment lives in jinja2.sandbox, not the jinja2 top level, so the module raises ImportError and every preview request - valid or missing-template - stops working, which the write-up does not say; the intended SandboxedEnvironment swap would otherwise have been the right fix.

R514.note: Five-character HTML entity escape with '&' first is correct for the body context, and the switch from format() to print() - which stops %s substitution from args {a,b} - is stated plainly and removes a format-string misuse rather than any legitimate feature.

R515.note: Rendering ticket.description as a JSX text child lets React escape it; the case comment says the field is plain free text returned unmodified, so no HTML formatting is lost, and the write-up states the plain-text treatment.

R516.note: Adding 'length > buffer_len - offset' after the existing offset check is overflow-safe and returns -1 before socket_send for any out-of-range slice, exactly per the contract, with in-range calls unchanged.

R517.note: resize(count) closes the out-of-bounds write into packet, but count is still never checked against fields.size(), so the same statement reads fields[i] out of bounds for large counts and the function returns garbage instead of rejecting or reporting the count as the contract requires.

R518.note: th:utext to th:text is the framework-native escape for a note rendered as text; the preview still shows the submitted note, now with markup rendered literally, which is the intended behaviour of a plain-text note preview.

R519.note: An allowlist map is the right shape for a user-named call_user_func_array, but the map's three command names and botHelp/botStatus/botReset targets are invented - none exist in the case and the original dispatched to a function named exactly as the command - so real commands may now be 'Unknown command' or fatal on an undefined function, and the write-up never says the developer must fill the map in.
